articles.title: South Africa moving ahead on new nuclear plans
articles.title_en: South Africa moving ahead on new nuclear plans
articles.excerpt: Energy Minister Kgosientsho Ramokgopa has said his department is preparing to put the case for an additional 5.2 GW of nuclear capacity in South Africa "before the public and will consider submissions on their merits".
bullets: The minister, pictured above speaking at the South African Nuclear and Clean Energy Conference last week, said state-owned Eskom had submitted its feasibility report for the extra capacity, which is scheduled to be on stream by 2039 under 2025’s Integrated Resource Plan.
The aim is for the final determination by the end of April 2027 "and then we will start the process of building 5.2 GW of nuclear", he said.
South Africa currently has two nuclear power reactors at Koeberg with a capacity of 1.85 GW, generating about 5% of the country's electricity.
The units entered commercial service in 1984 and 1985 respectively.

articles.title: Nuclea Energy concludes Moltex acquisition
articles.title_en: Nuclea Energy concludes Moltex acquisition
articles.excerpt: Nuclea Energy has concluded its acquisition of Moltex Energy Limited's technology and intellectual property portfolio, adding the WATSS used nuclear fuel recycling technology and the SSR-W small modular reactor design to Nuclea's portfolio which already includes the Morpheus lead-cooled microreactor design.
bullets: The transaction was executed through the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Nuclea Energy Canada Inc, following the satisfaction of all customary closing conditions on 17 November, the companies said.

The core technology has been successfully tested at Canadian Nuclear Laboratories using real used nuclear fuel, and has been shown to recover more than 90% of the transuranic elements from legacy CANDU fuel, producing a liquid chloride fuel salt which can be used to produce fuel for many types of advanced reactors.
This could reduce deep geological disposal of high-level nuclear waste volumes by up to 95%, the companies said.
The 300 to 500 MWe fast-spectrum molten salt reactor is designed for on-grid baseload power, using the recycled WATSS fuel.

articles.title: Energy crisis reinforces comeback of nuclear power, says IEA
articles.title_en: Energy crisis reinforces comeback of nuclear power, says IEA
articles.excerpt:
Unprecedented disruption in the energy world - primarily resulting from the war in the Middle East - is set to reinforce the comeback of nuclear power, according to the International Energy Agency's latest
World Energy Outlook
, which has revised its forecast for nuclear upwards.
bullets: The IEA says the global energy system has shown "considerable resilience" in the face of cumulative losses of 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic metres of gas supply from the Gulf, but increasingly it is falling to consumers - and high prices - to absorb the impact as other buffers are run down.
"In an echo of the 1970s, the 2026 crisis is set to reinforce the comeback of nuclear power," the IEA says.

It notes that, as of mid-year, nearly 90 GW of new nuclear capacity was under construction - the highest level for more than 35 years, and more than 50 countries now have plans or targets for nuclear power, including new technologies such as small modular reactors.
"Nuclear power generation has been revised upwards compared with the World Energy Outlook 2025 , with much of the upside in China and the United States," the IEA said.

articles.title: Hot and cold testing under way for Turkey's Akkuyu 1
articles.title_en: Hot and cold testing under way for Turkey's Akkuyu 1
articles.excerpt: The first nuclear power reactor in Turkey has moved a step closer to start-up, with hot and cold commissioning tests taking place.
bullets: Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant's unit 1 will have all its equipment in the primary and secondary circuits tested under operating conditions - with checks of equipment strength, piping, vibration, safety systems, reactor control and protection systems.

The commissioning programme involves "gradually warming up the reactor unit and increasing the temperature and pressure of the primary coolant (desalinated water) to their rated values of 285°C and 16.5 MPa.

articles.excerpt: The search for a site for Estonia's first nuclear power plant will now focus on three locations, all in the municipality of Viru-Nigula, about 120 kilometres east of Tallin, after three locations in Lüganuse municipality were ruled out for security reasons.
bullets: The Estonian Government initiated the state spatial planning process for the nuclear power plant at the request of Fermi Energia in May 2025.

The first part of the phased planning process - site pre-selection - is taking place up to 2027, focusing on promising areas near the village of Kunda in Viru-Nigula and the village of Aa in Lüganuse.
This collaboration built upon a memorandum of understanding signed between the two companies in November 2024.

articles.title: Cernavodă units returning to operation after three months
articles.title_en: Cernavodă units returning to operation after three months
articles.excerpt: Nuclearelectrica and the Romanian government are working on long-term solutions to avoid a repeat of the Cernavodă units being shut down because of drought causing abnormally low water levels in the Danube.
bullets: The first unit was reconnected to the grid on Friday 6 November, with unit 2 undergoing start-up work on Monday.

Unit 1 was shut down at the end of July, with the second unit shut in early August as precautions as drought in central Europe saw the river Danube's water level drop too low to provide the required amount of cooling water for the units to be kept in operation.
The historically low water levels - lower than designers had envisaged happening in 100 years - also had an impact on nuclear power plants in Hungary and Bulgaria.
It will provide water for cooling, both to units 1 and 2, and to those that will be built - units 3 and 4.

articles.title: China Pours First Concrete For HTGR At ‘World’s First’ Hybrid Nuclear Power Station
articles.title_en: China Pours First Concrete For HTGR At ‘World’s First’ Hybrid Nuclear Power Station
articles.excerpt:
The first batch of concrete has been poured for the nuclear island of the high-temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR) that forms part the first phase of a hybrid nuclear power station in Jiangsu province, eastern China.

The facility, known as the Jiangsu Xuwei Nuclear Heating and Power Plant, will supply both industrial heat and electricity by coupling the Chilong One HTGR with two Hualong One pressurised water reactors (PWRs).

CNNC said first concrete had now been poured for the 600-MW HTGR. That follows the pouring of first concrete in January for the nuclear island of Unit 1, a Hualong One
bullets: CNNC said first concrete had now been poured for the 600-MW HTGR.
The Hualong One, also known as the HPR1000, is a 1,000-MW plant that combines features from China National Nuclear Corporation’s (CNNC) ACP1000 and CGN’s ACPR1000+ designs.
In its official reactor database, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) lists Unit 1 as being under construction, but has not yet listed the second Hualong One (Unit 2) or the HTGR (Unit 3).
According to the IAEA, China has 60 nuclear units in commercial operation and 37 under construction.

articles.title: Canadian budget sets out nuclear investments
articles.title_en: Canadian budget sets out nuclear investments
articles.excerpt: The budget released by the Canadian government provides funding for a strategy to double grid capacity by 2050, as well as investments in nuclear energy and critical minerals.
bullets: The Nuclear Energy Strategy was presented by the government in June, setting out a plan to grow the sector by unlocking investment, modernising regulation, strengthening Canadian research and development, and promoting Canadian nuclear expertise abroad.

"To implement key commitments under the strategy, Budget 2026 proposes to provide CAD518.5 million over five years, starting in 2027-28, and CAD18.1 million ongoing to advance Canada’s nuclear research, supply chains, workforce, and regulatory capacity," the Budget notes.
Up to CAD3 billion of export financing has also been made available for the construction of two new CANDU reactors in Romania.

Budget 2026 builds on those strengths by unlocking investment, building more at home, strengthening our energy and natural resource advantage, and helping Canadian businesses grow and compete on the world stage.

articles.title: ASNR opens passive safety system testing facility
articles.title_en: ASNR opens passive safety system testing facility
articles.excerpt: France's nuclear safety regulator has inaugurated new research infrastructure and facilities at its Cadarache site for studying the reliability of passive safety systems. It aims to generate the scientific knowledge necessary for the independent safety assessment of innovative reactors and small modular reactors.
bullets: Passive safety systems aim to bring a reactor to a safe shutdown state and maintain this state for a long period of time without the need for human intervention and with limited reliance on support functions.

One of the avenues of development and innovation being pursued by nuclear power plant designers and operators is the integration of passive systems into new-generation reactors, including small modular reactors (SMRs).
With funding of EUR9 million (USD10 million) by the French government as part of the France 2030 initiative, the PASTIS project provides the ASNR with a leading scientific tool.
"State support within the framework of France 2030 was crucial in bringing PASTIS to fruition," said Sébastien Desmarest, PASTIS project manager.

articles.title_en: Concrete work completed for Akkuyu 4's turbine unit

bullets: More than 308 tonnes of rebar was installed beforehand.
It will take an estimated 60 days before the foundation reaches its design strength.
When the 4,800 MWe plant is completed, it is expected to meet about 10% of Turkey's electricity needs.

articles.title: Construction of Chinese HTGR begins
articles.title_en: Construction of Chinese HTGR begins
articles.excerpt: The first batch of concrete has been poured for the nuclear island of the high-temperature gas-cooled reactor that forms part of the initial phase of the Jiangsu Xuwei Nuclear Heating and Power Plant, China National Nuclear Corporation has announced.
bullets: Xuwei Phase I was among 11 reactors approved by China's State Council in August 2024.

China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC) plans to build two 1,208 MWe (net) Hualong One (HPR1000) pressurised water reactors (units 1 and 2) and one 660 MWe high-temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR) (unit 3) at the site in Lianyungang, Jiangsu province.
The unit has a rated capacity of 660 MWe and is designed for an operational lifespan of 60 years.

bullets: Calogena - a subsidiary of Group Gorgé founded in 2021 - is developing a water-cooled small modular reactor (SMR), called the CAL30, with a thermal power of 30 MW, specifically designed to supply urban heating networks with carbon-free energy.

bullets: An international coalition of nuclear industry and professional organisations has called on the Cop31 climate summit presidency to include nuclear energy in its implementation and financing plans, ahead of the summit in Turkey later this month.

Nuclear for Climate (N4C), an initiative of nuclear professionals, engineers and scientists established in 2015 by more than 150 associations worldwide, said that existing political recognition must be followed by concrete measures to support projects.

N4C said 41 organisations representing more than 100,000 nuclear professionals and other stakeholders had signed the letter to Cop31 president-designate Murat Kurum, Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanisation and climate change.

articles.title: World Nuclear Association calls for internationally aligned regulation at IAEA ministerial conference

The conference brings together ministers, policymakers and international experts to explore how nuclear power can meet growing energy demand, strengthen energy security and support climate goals and sustainable development.

Discussions cover the foundations for successful nuclear programmes, regulatory effectiveness, advanced technologies, workforce development and supply chains, and emerging applications of nuclear power.
